reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-level context, the full `SubstanceProtein` StructureDefinition report, the direct HTTP REST behavior finding, shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context, the deterministic aggregate as prior context, R4 maturity metadata, and the local R4/R6 core package definitions. The local package check confirmed that R4 defines `SubstanceProtein` as a concrete resource with protein sequence/subunit fields and that the supplied R6 package has no `StructureDefinition-SubstanceProtein.json`; `SubstanceDefinition` is the plausible successor area but does not expose same-name protein subunit fields.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `SubstanceProtein` is trial-use/FMM 0, so the compatibility burden is materially lower than for mature or normative resources. That weakens the case for retaining a separate legacy resource identity in R6, but it does not eliminate concern about regulated medicinal-substance data if migration loses computable protein sequence, subunit, disulfide, or terminal-modification meaning.

overall.oneLineConclusion: `SubstanceProtein` requires a resource-level migration to the R6 substance model, but R6 should still preserve protein-specific semantics through low-cost successor guidance, mappings, profiles, or optional elements where feasible.

reasoning.thesisMd: This is not a mostly stable resource with isolated element churn. The same-named R6 resource is absent, so every R4 `SubstanceProtein` instance, generated model, route, search surface, and reference assumption needs a resource-level migration decision before element-level validation can succeed. The most plausible R6 direction is consolidation into `SubstanceDefinition`, but the important residual issue is whether protein-specific computable content survives that consolidation.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration shape is a removed/replaced resource. The R4 definition describes a specialized protein substance resource with fields such as `sequenceType`, `numberOfSubunits`, `disulfideLinkage`, and repeating `subunit` details. The supplied R6 package contains `SubstanceDefinition` and `Substance`, but no `SubstanceProtein` resource. R6 `SubstanceDefinition` has generic `property` and `structure.representation` slots and an IDMP mapping, but no direct named counterpart for the R4 protein subunit model. That makes migration a governed model consolidation rather than a same-path rename.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: A major migration program is unavoidable, but that does not mean all additional compatibility work is wasted. Preserving the old `SubstanceProtein` resource type or endpoint as a base R6 alias is not clearly low-cost for an FMM 0 draft resource because it would keep a parallel resource family alive. By contrast, providing official successor guidance, a computable cross-version map, a standard profile/extension package, or optional protein-specific structure inside `SubstanceDefinition` could materially reduce lossy migration without undoing the consolidation.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The low-leverage alternative is keeping the entire legacy resource identity in base R6; that would preserve wire compatibility but at high model, endpoint, search, validator, and codegen cost. The higher-value less-breaking alternative is narrower: preserve named protein semantics in the successor model or in an official companion mapping/profile so sequence, subunit, disulfide, and terminal-modification data do not become local free text or implementation-specific properties.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct HTTP REST behavior finding is real for `SubstanceProtein` because the base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises the old resource endpoint among many removed resources. For this resource, however, that endpoint break is derivative of the resource removal and does not independently change the conclusion. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only because `SubstanceProtein` is neither `Resource` nor `DomainResource`.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate that major migration is unavoidable and that the migration shape is a removed/replaced resource. I do not reduce the standards posture all the way to pure `migration-program-dominates`: the protein-specific mapping finding remains standards-review-worthy because relatively narrow successor-model guidance or optional structures could preserve high-value semantics even though the old resource identity is gone.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The supplied reports did not include an official HL7 R4-to-R6 change note, ConceptMap, StructureMap, or final successor profile for `SubstanceProtein`. Confidence is high in the resource-removal conclusion and in the absence of direct same-name protein fields in the inspected R6 package; confidence is lower in the exact intended migration target and the best standards vehicle for preserving protein-specific semantics.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 core package no longer defines the SubstanceProtein resource
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the decisive resource-level break. A valid R4 instance with `resourceType: "SubstanceProtein"` has no same-named R6 core StructureDefinition, so migration must address resource identity, validators, generated models, endpoints, persistence discriminators, and references before local element compatibility can matter. Because the R4 artifact is FMM 0/trial-use, retaining the whole legacy resource identity is not clearly a low-cost base-compatibility obligation.

findingConsiderations.title: Protein-specific sequence and subunit fields have no direct R6 SubstanceDefinition counterpart
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This finding prevents the review from treating the resource removal as merely an accepted local chore. The old fields are central to protein substance identity and may be regulatory or product-definition critical. Even when migration to `SubstanceDefinition` is accepted, the lack of named successor slots or an official map risks lossy, expert-dependent migration; this is the main reason compatibility preservation still has leverage.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This direct behavior finding applies to `SubstanceProtein`, but for this resource it is a consequence of the same resource lifecycle decision already captured by the StructureDefinition identity break. It matters operationally for route inventories and generic conformance tooling, but it does not make the migration broader than the removed-resource conclusion already does.

findingConsiderations.title: Required input parameter renamed from `input` to `resource`
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The shared `Resource/$convert` API would be relevant to cross-version conversion tooling, but it is shared Resource behavior rather than a `SubstanceProtein`-specific break. It reinforces the need for explicit conversion guidance without being scored as a resource-level `SubstanceProtein` migration driver.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource/DomainResource search-parameter metadata change may affect generic clients, but it is not specific to the removed `SubstanceProtein` resource. It remains background context only under the resource-review scope.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish or validate an official R4 `SubstanceProtein` to R6 `SubstanceDefinition` migration map, including explicit handling for `sequenceType`, `numberOfSubunits`, `disulfideLinkage`, and all `subunit` sequence and terminal-modification fields.

Review whether R6 `SubstanceDefinition` should include a standard protein-specific backbone, optional elements, or a companion profile/extension package so regulated protein identity data has stable computable target paths.

Document endpoint and search transition expectations for implementations that exposed R4 `SubstanceProtein`, making clear whether legacy routes are purely implementation-specific compatibility features.
Do not prioritize preserving the full old `SubstanceProtein` resource identity in base R6 unless new implementation evidence shows substantial active dependence on the FMM 0 draft resource.

caveats: No official R4-to-R6 change note or committee rationale for the `SubstanceProtein` removal was available in the local inputs.
No official ConceptMap, StructureMap, cross-version extension package, or R6 protein profile was available to prove a lossless migration path.
The R6 input is a ballot package, so the final R6 substance model or migration guidance may change.
